title: Toolchain parity gate: maintenance and automation for fallback model variants
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background: Smart routing relies on a fast, deterministic fallback mechanism that can route requests to compatible model variants when primary capacity or region constraints are hit. Over the past two quarters we have accumulated ad-hoc mappings and one-off fixes for tokenizer differences, context window handling, and tool-calling ABIs. This has increased incident risk and blocked several canary rollouts.

Goal: Create and maintain a single source of truth 'parity gate' that codifies tokenizer compatibility, context/KV cache serialization schemas, prompt+tool ABI expectations, and allowed quantization/precision boundaries for every model variant we will consider as automatic fallbacks. Automate daily validations and gating checks that feed into routing decisions.

Scope:
- Inventory: canonicalize model metadata fields used by the runtime (tokenizer_id, vocab_hash, ctx_window, kv_blob_version, tool_abi_version, float_precision_tag).
- Validation: implement a CI pipeline that launches lightweight compatibility tests for new variants (tokenization roundtrip, prefix-KV rehydration, tool-call marshaling).
- Automation: implement a cron job and webhook-based sync that refreshes the compatibility ledger and emits alerts on drift.
- Back-compat remediation: define automated fallback transformations (e.g., tokenizer mapping layers, kv-compat adapters) when safe, and escalation paths when not.
- Runtime integration: add a parity-check step to the smart router that can reject an automatic fallback if the parity gate is not green; provide an override API for SRE/Oncall in emergencies.

Out of scope: deep model conversion tooling, wholesale model retraining, or manual tokenization fixes for third-party models (these will be handled via vendor engagement).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Compatibility ledger stored in the config service, with documented fields and a stable JSON schema.
2) Daily validation runs with dashboarded pass/fail rate; failures create JIRA/Linear tickets automatically for affected models.
3) Smart router consults parity gate and will not route to a variant that fails critical checks (tokenizer mismatch, KV schema incompatible).
4) Automated adapter exists for the common tokenizer mapping case (>=90% coverage for our top-15 fallback variants).
5) Runbook and rollback plan for incidents where automated gating prevents expected fallback behavior.

Metrics:
- Reduction in fallback-induced production errors (target 60% reduction in errors attributed to variant incompatibility within 8 weeks).
- Time to detect a drift in ledger (target < 1 hour from upstream change).
- Percentage of fallback decisions blocked by parity gate that require manual intervention (target < 10%).

Rollout plan:
- Week 1-2: implement ledger schema + inventory import; smoke tests for top-5 variants.
- Week 3: CI validation pipeline and dashboard (Grafana panel + metric tags).
- Week 4: integrate parity-check in the router with a conservative default (log-only).
- Week 5: flip to enforcement in canary region (us-west-2), monitor.
- Week 6: global enforcement, add oncall overrides and complete runbook.

Risks & trade-offs:
- False positives in validation could reduce available capacity temporarily; mitigated by staged enforcement and overrides.
- Adding a parity-check adds latency to routing decisions; mitigate by caching gate decisions and TTL-based freshness.

Docs & artifacts: canonical spec in Drive (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ParityGateSpec), design PR draft (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6712), initial dashboard (https://grafana.redwood.com/d/variant-parity/ledger-health).
